James Clerk Maxwell (1831–1879) was a Scottish physicist whose revolutionary work laid the groundwork for modern physics. He is best known for formulating the classical theory of electromagnetism, distilled into his famous set of equations that unified electricity, magnetism, and light into a single electromagnetic field. Beyond electromagnetism, Maxwell made pioneering contributions to the kinetic theory of gases, color vision, and optics, and his insights directly inspired later breakthroughs like Einstein’s theory of relativity. Today, he is widely celebrated as one of the most influential scientists in history.
